text:
lina_support: customer reported console shows 3-4 hour lag in hourly usage and some tenants have zeros for recent windows :frowning: they say graphs stopped updating around 21:10 UTC
adam_cs: they're on tier 'acme-inc', started seeing it ~21:05, reported missing rows for 21:00-22:00 window
lina_support: repro steps from customer: open console -> tenant hours -> last 3 hrs -> chart shows last datapoint at 20:00
devon_eng: thanks. can you paste the tenant id and a request id if they have one? also which region?
adam_cs: tenant=acme-123, region=us-west-2, sample request ids: req_2026_03_17_2109_azb
devon_eng: I ran the query against the hourly_rollups table and the rows after 20:00 are missing for that tenant. looks like the ETL backfill didn't process those partitions.
maria_analytics: I see the backfill job for hourly-rollups in our pipeline attempted retries and then throttled out. consumer lag jumped around 21:00. suspect connector -> s3 manifest sync flapped, leaving tombstoned batches unprocessed.
maria_analytics: log excerpt from etl-worker-3 at 21:12:
```
2026-03-17T21:12:03Z ERROR consumer: partition 42: offset out of range (expected 12034, found 11000)
2026-03-17T21:12:04Z WARN s3-manifest: missing objects for manifest job 8f3a, marking for retry
2026-03-17T21:12:04Z ERROR backfill-scheduler: backoff exceeded for job-hourly-2026-03-17-21, giving up
```

devon_eng: that explains it. connector retries hit the per-task backoff cap and the scheduler marked the window as failed instead of requeuing. we have a fix in a PR to make retries durable and requeue on manifest missing.
lina_support: customer asked for ETA to show data again, any quick mitigation?
devon_eng: short-term: manually requeue the hourly window for the tenant and restart the etl-worker on that shard. steps:
```
# requeue specific window
python tools/etl_requeue.py --date 2026-03-17 --hour 21 --tenant acme-123
# restart worker safely
kubectl rollout restart deployment/etl-worker-3 -n analytics
```

sachin_oncall: I'm on it, will perform restart and requeue now. tagging eng-infra in case K8s node issues show up. @devon_eng please stand by. :eyes:
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout restart for deployment/etl-worker-3 by sachin_oncall at 2026-03-17T21:28:00Z, track: RB-4591
sachin_oncall: requeue task completed, pod restart initiated. seeing consumer group rebalance. monitoring lag.
analytics-bot: backfill job job-hourly-2026-03-17-21 requeued by sachin_oncall, status=queued, estimate=~18m
maria_analytics: kicked off a targeted backfill for acme-123 across partition set 40-45 to avoid full cluster reprocess. also applying temp increase to connector retry cap.
analytics-bot: backfill progress: 25% -> 60% (2026-03-17T21:45:00Z)
devon_eng: checking console query caches — we might still show stale charts until prefix cache invalidates. flush cache for route /v1/console/hours for tenant acme-123
lina_support: done that flush after backfill started, told customer about ETA ~30-40m.
analytics-bot: backfill progress: 95% -> complete (2026-03-17T22:12:00Z). rows written for 21:00 window.
maria_analytics: verified row counts and rollup sums match expected. I also opened PR 6432 to change backoff behaviour; will promote to canary tomorrow.
devon_eng: console now shows updated datapoints for acme-123 for 21:00-22:00, confirmed with sample queries. I'll leave the ticket open for a few hours to validate.
adam_cs: customer confirmed charts are back and says thanks. noted the incident and that we applied a manual requeue + worker restart.
lina_support: root cause summary to include in ticket: etl-worker hit manifest missing errors, retries capped and window marked failed -> manual requeue + worker restart resolved; mitigation: increase retry/durable requeue and PR 6432 to change scheduler behaviour.
sachin_oncall: putting follow-up checklist: monitor connector error rate, watch consumer lag for 6hrs, promote PR to canary.
lina_support: thanks everyone. closing customer-facing update. :white_check_mark:
